purpose: This medication combines two hormones, estrogen and a small amount of testosterone, to help relieve symptoms of menopause such as hot flashes and decreased sex drive. It is typically used when estrogen alone has not fully helped with menopausal symptoms. Doctors may prescribe it specifically when low sexual desire is a concern during menopause.
how_it_works: Estrogen replaces the hormone your body makes less of after menopause, helping to balance your hormone levels and ease symptoms like hot flashes and vaginal dryness. The small amount of testosterone (methyltestosterone) in this medicine helps boost energy and sexual desire, which can decrease during menopause. Together, these two hormones work as a team to help you feel more like yourself again.
common_side_effects: Nausea, bloating, breast tenderness or swelling, headaches, mood changes, acne, mild unwanted hair growth, and changes in your menstrual cycle. Some people may notice a deeper voice or oily skin due to the testosterone component.
warnings: This medication carries serious risks including increased chance of blood clots, stroke, heart attack, and certain cancers such as breast and uterine cancer. It should not be used if you are pregnant, have a history of hormone-sensitive cancers, blood clotting disorders, or liver problems. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and medications before taking this. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed, and see your doctor regularly for checkups.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day, often the lowest strength available (half-strength tablets are also available). Your doctor will choose the dose that works best for you. It is often taken cyclically, meaning you take it for three weeks and then take a break for one week, though your doctor may adjust this schedule for your needs.
